[33m#S3[0m Add microsecond support to ms (`us`, `µs`, `microsecond`, `microseconds`) so `ms("500us")` returns 0.5, with updated unit types, README unit list, and tests (Nov 2, 8:07 PM)


[34mInvestigated:[0m The ms repository layout and src/index.ts parser: unit type unions, the parse regex, the parse switch with its `satisfies never` check, the README unit list, and the existing test files (parse.test.ts, parse-strict.test.ts, format.test.ts, index.test.ts).

[33mLearned:[0m Units are declared as string-literal unions, matched by a single regex in parse(), and mapped in a switch to millisecond constants. A scripted replacement anchored on a leading pipe silently failed because the regex begins with `(?<unit>`, which left the first test run returning NaN for microsecond input. A sed edit on the `<unit>milliseconds?` anchor fixed it.

[32mCompleted:[0m Added a Microseconds type (`'microseconds' | 'microsecond' | 'µs' | 'us'`) to the Unit union in src/index.ts. Added the microsecond alternatives to the parse regex and a switch case returning n / 1000. Added a Greek mu (μs, U+03BC) case, since lowercasing the uppercase form produces it. Added the Microseconds type to the README units list. Added microsecond tests to src/parse.test.ts and a parseStrict case to src/parse-strict.test.ts. Verified with npx tsc --noEmit (clean), npx jest (171 passed, 100% coverage on index.ts), and npx biome check src (no issues).

[35mNext Steps:[0m Final review of the diff. The reported summary also notes that ms(0.5) still formats as "0.5ms" rather than switching to microseconds; that formatting behavior is intentionally unchanged and not part of the current request.

[36mNotes:[0m Two Greek-letter variants were handled deliberately: the micro sign (U+00B5) and the Greek mu (U+03BC). The case-insensitive regex flag and toLowerCase() can produce either form, which is why the matchUnit cast was widened. Earlier failures were a single root cause in the regex, not the type or switch changes.
